text:
The Flyers arrive in Edmonton with their season's biggest question hanging over them, and it isn't the standings. Kevin Weekes reported that Matvei Michkov wants "a new start elsewhere," after weeks of headlines about his ice time, and PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor says the Flyers didn't know before the report broke. Michkov was the centerpiece of their 2023 draft and, as O'Connor put it, "arguably the key piece" of the rebuild. How Philadelphia handles a 21-year-old who wants out matters more than tonight, but tonight is the first chance to see how he plays with it in the air. He has been shooting above his chances, and he set up Travis Konecny's power-play goal in Vancouver on Monday.

The Flyers have the hardest underlying numbers to defend in this matchup: 42% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) on the season. They snapped a three-game winless run with that 3-1 win in Vancouver, game three of a five-game road trip. Konecny and Owen Tippett are back from injuries, and Dan Vladar starts.

Edmonton is the other kind of story. Connor McDavid has a point in all 19 games to start the season (11 goals, 37 assists). Leon Draisaitl has scored in four straight. The Oilers are +23 in goal difference on chances worth +3.7, which means they have finished 20.4 goals better than usual. Some of that is McDavid and Draisaitl being who they are; not all of it will last. Devon Levi stole Monday's win over the Rangers, 2.6 goals better than the shots deserved, and he starts again.

Our numbers give Edmonton 3.1 expected goals to Philadelphia's 2.6. McDavid is 94% for a point by our count, which is about as close to certain as hockey gets.
headline: Michkov wants a new start. Edmonton is next.

hunch.text: A player with every reason to make a point on the ice, against a team that has given up chances all season. Our gut says Michkov scores.
